summary: Repository schedulers and dependency/security automation provide mature primitives for periodic whole-system sweeps. They become this pattern when each run has named ownership, bounded scope, a comparable result schema and durable follow-up rather than merely a cron expression.

items.text: GitHub Actions workflow syntax supports cron-based schedule triggers, timezone-aware schedules and manual invocation, executing from the latest default-branch commit. A repository can use one named workflow per sweep and publish standardized check outputs and artifacts.

GitHub CodeQL default setup scans code on a schedule in addition to push and pull-request events, catching vulnerabilities outside the immediate change path. Results become durable code-scanning alerts with rule and location evidence.

Dependabot configuration supports daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, semiannual and annual update intervals, grouping and per-ecosystem directories. It implements a recurring dependency-freshness sweep with explicit scope and generated remediation changes.

Renovate's schedule configuration constrains when repository update checks and branch creation occur and supports named presets. Its dependency dashboard and PR artifacts turn detected staleness into owned follow-up work.
